note.question: How do supplier centrality and auditing priority interact in socially responsible supply chains?
note.overview: A key question in socially responsible supply networks is as follows: When firms audit some, but not all, of their respective suppliers, how do the degree centralities of the suppliers (i.e., the number of firms to which they supply) affect their auditing priority from the viewpoint of the firms? To investigate, we consider an assembly network consisting of two firms and three suppliers; each firm has one independent supplier that uniquely supplies to that firm and one common supplier that supplies to both. To mitigate this impact, firms preemptively audit suppliers although resource and time considerations typically restrict the number of suppliers a firm can audit.

We show that this inefficiency is corrected when the firms cooperate (via a stable coalition) to jointly audit the suppliers and share the auditing cost in a fair manner.

Our work is also related to studies that examine the practice of joint auditing in socially responsible supply chains in which multiple buyers share one supplier: Fang and Cho (2016) address cooperation among multiple manufacturers in jointly auditing a common supplier.
